steps.calloutTitle: Riya's compliance workbench · every regulatory obligation, one queue
steps.calloutText: Every loan Riya owns, with ESDD, taxonomy, CAP, and monitoring status visible on one row. Follow-up reminders surface anything due this week.
steps.narration: Welcome. This is the compliance workbench built for First Bank of Nepal. Riya Sharma is a loan officer. Her queue shows every loan the bank has assigned to her, with every regulatory obligation on one row. Circular twenty-two environmental screening. Green Finance Taxonomy classification. Corrective action plan status. Monitoring cadence. Over the next seven minutes I will walk you through how Riya takes one commercial loan through the entire NRB compliance lifecycle from a new application to a defensible audit trail.

steps.calloutText: CAP items due, monitoring reports due, covenant checks due — all rolled up at the top of Riya's queue.
steps.narration: Above the queue is the follow-up reminder panel. Any corrective action item, any monitoring report, or any covenant check that is due this week surfaces here with the borrower name and the number of days remaining. Circular twenty-two section seven point three point seven treats missed monitoring as a compliance breach, not an administrative oversight. This panel is how Riya makes sure that never happens on her book.

steps.calloutTitle: One loan · every flow visible before Riya clicks in
steps.calloutText: ESDD status. Taxonomy classification. CAP status. Escalation flag. NRB requires ESRM before taxonomy, so ESDD is always Riya's entry point.
steps.narration: Each card in Riya's queue is one loan. She sees at a glance where every regulatory flow stands. The ESDD checklist progress, the taxonomy classification if the sector is eligible, and any corrective action items or covenants attached to the loan. Green Finance Taxonomy section three point two point two requires ESRM screening to be complete before taxonomy classification. So the ESDD action button is always the officer's entry point. Everything else unlocks in the correct sequence.

steps.calloutText: Prefilled from the loan record. NRB Circular 22 requires these fields at the top of every checklist.
steps.narration: When Riya opens the ESDD, the first step is basic information. Date, transaction ID, client name, industry, loan category, location. All prefilled from the loan record. Circular twenty-two requires these fields at the top of every screening file. She confirms and moves on.

steps.calloutText: Three questions on legal issues, stakeholder grievances, and eco-sensitive-area siting. Verbatim Circular 22 language.
steps.narration: Section one. General risk. Three questions on legal permits and standing, stakeholder grievances or media coverage, and whether the site sits near protected or eco-sensitive areas. Each question offers four options. A is the best case. B is partial mitigation with a plan. C is an unmitigated concern that will trigger escalation. D is not applicable. The wording matches Circular twenty-two verbatim so the audit trail is defensible.

steps.calloutText: Five questions on air, water, land, energy, and climate risk. Evidence uploads live on every remarks field.
steps.narration: Section two. Environmental health and safety. Five questions on air and noise pollution, water pollution, land pollution and waste handling, energy efficiency or renewables, and climate change risks and opportunities. The climate question was added in the twenty twenty two update to reflect NGFS climate risk taxonomy. Every question includes NRB's own guidance notes and a remarks field. Riya can attach the underlying source document, an EIA extract, a monitoring report, a photograph, directly on the remarks field. When the auditor asks how she reached a conclusion, the evidence is one click away.

steps.calloutTitle: Section 3 · Social risks · the escalation triggers
steps.calloutText: Four questions on occupational H&S, labour, community H&S, and stakeholder consultation. Two 'c' answers here route the loan to credit committee.
steps.narration: Section three. Social risks. Four questions on occupational health and safety, labour practices, community health and safety, and stakeholder consultation with Indigenous Peoples. On this loan the officer recorded a c answer to labour practices and another to community health and safety. Those two answers are what will trigger the credit committee escalation you saw on the queue. Every answer auto-saves with a timestamp and Riya's officer identity attached.

steps.calloutTitle: Review · computed risk class and recommendation
steps.calloutText: Scoring engine derives risk class. Escalation banner surfaces the driving questions. Recommendation calls for CAP + covenants.
steps.narration: The review step. The scoring engine runs the NRB rules over Riya's answers and returns a risk class. On this loan the two c answers in section three drive the classification. The rationale text spells out exactly why. The recommendation is approve with conditions, binding covenants on the flagged items, and quarterly monitoring. That recommendation is not just a note. It becomes the source for the corrective action plan on the next surface.

steps.calloutTitle: CAP + Covenants + Monitoring · §7.3.5 and §7.3.7 in one panel
steps.calloutText: Corrective actions with deadlines. Covenants written into the facility agreement. Monitoring reports on cadence.
steps.narration: Circular twenty-two section seven point three point five says every medium and high risk loan needs a time-bound corrective action plan with covenants. Section seven point three point seven says those actions need periodic monitoring. Both live on this panel. Riya lists each corrective action with its deadline and its owner, records the covenants exactly as they were negotiated into the facility agreement, and sets the monitoring cadence. When a deadline slips, the loan flags on Riya's queue and on the manager's portfolio banner. This is the piece that turns a screening into an ongoing obligation.

steps.calloutTitle: Green Finance Taxonomy · choose the applicable activity
steps.calloutText: Seventeen activities encoded from NRB Oct 2024. Suggested activities appear first based on the borrower's sector.
steps.narration: Now the taxonomy wizard. The screening is saved, so the taxonomy classification unlocks. Step two is activity selection. The wizard suggests activities based on the borrower's sector. Seventeen activities are encoded from the October twenty twenty four directive covering every case Nepal banks commonly underwrite. Hydropower classified on lifecycle emissions. Utility solar and wind. Cement, which has no fully green pathway and lands on amber or excluded. Green buildings against LEED or EDGE. Poultry, dairy, aquaculture. Textiles. Hotels. Waste management. Consumer EV loans. And the fossil fuel exclusion.

steps.calloutTitle: Classification result · Green, Amber, Red, with DNSH
steps.calloutText: Live preview of the derivation. Save records the classification, rationale, and NRB citation to the audit trail.
steps.narration: The taxonomy review step. The classifier returns green, amber, or red with any Do No Significant Harm failures called out separately. DNSH is the principle that says an activity cannot count as green if it materially harms another environmental objective. Water. Biodiversity. Community rights. Climate adaptation. Cement on this loan lands on amber, transitional financing, because it remains a hard-to-abate sector with no fully green pathway under NRB's own methodology. The saved classification carries the rationale text and the NRB citation.

steps.calloutTitle: PCAF Data Availability · what the NFRS auditor asks first
steps.calloutText: Four flag rows for the PCAF option ladder. Auto-inferred from the borrower record, confirmed by Riya, flipped to MANUAL when overridden.
steps.narration: One more panel before Riya moves on. PCAF Data Availability. This is what the NFRS auditor asks about first. Four flag rows corresponding to the PCAF option ladder. Verified reported emissions. Unverified reported. Physical activity data. Revenue-only. The starting state is auto-inferred from what the borrower record already contains. When Riya changes a flag, the badge flips from AUTO to MANUAL and the evidence field records why. That is how the financed emissions score for this loan becomes defensible when it rolls up into the annual NFRS filing.

steps.calloutTitle: Every flow saved · the manager sees it immediately
steps.calloutText: Risk chip · Amber classification · CAP status · PCAF availability. All from one workflow.
steps.narration: Back in her queue. The loan card now shows every regulatory decision. The environmental risk class on the ESDD side. The amber classification on the taxonomy side. The corrective action items scheduled with deadlines. The PCAF availability captured. The manager's view updates immediately because both surfaces read from the same records. Riya moves on to her next loan.

steps.calloutTitle: One loan · one workflow · every NRB layer
steps.calloutText: Circular 22. Green Finance Taxonomy. CAP + covenants + monitoring. PCAF availability. Every capture officer-attributed and timestamped.
steps.narration: That is the officer workflow. Every NRB layer captured in the correct sequence, every answer attributed to Riya's officer identity, every classification carrying its citation, every corrective action with a deadline that the follow-up surface will remind her about. When the compliance manager reviews her work, or NRB examines the loan three years from now, the audit trail is complete. Thanks for watching.
